name: libSQL
tagline: Turso's open-contribution SQLite fork with native vectors, a network server and embedded replicas.
description: libSQL is an open-source, open-contribution fork of SQLite created by Turso (formerly ChiselStrike) in 2022, because upstream SQLite does not accept outside patches. It keeps the SQLite file format and C API while adding a network server (sqld) with HTTP and WebSocket protocols, embedded replicas that sync a local copy from a remote primary, native vector columns with DiskANN indexes, ALTER TABLE extensions and WASM user-defined functions. It powers the classic Turso Cloud and many edge deployments. Turso now points new projects to Turso Database, its Rust rewrite, so libSQL receives fixes and occasional releases rather than major new features.
statusNote: Turso has shifted development to Turso Database (Rust rewrite) and recommends it for new projects; libSQL still gets fixes and releases (0.10.0, Oct 2026).

pricing.notes: Library and server are MIT; Turso Cloud hosts libSQL databases with a free tier.

scale.notes: Single primary per database; scale by using many small databases (per tenant) and embedded read replicas.

strengths: Drop-in SQLite compatibility with a network server added
Embedded replicas give microsecond local reads synced from a remote primary
Native vector type and ANN index without extensions
Open to outside contributions, unlike upstream SQLite
Database-per-tenant pattern is cheap and practical
weaknesses: Development focus has moved to Turso Database
Divergence from upstream SQLite means extensions and tools may lag
Self-hosted sqld has less documentation than Turso Cloud
useCases: Edge and serverless apps needing SQLite over the network
Local-first apps with synced embedded replicas
Small RAG and semantic-search apps using native vectors
notIdealFor: New greenfield projects (Turso recommends Turso Database)
